message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it might be a STEMI, right?
reply:
**There are anterior ST–T changes, but I wouldn’t call this a definite STEMI from this image alone.**

My reading:

- Regular sinus rhythm, approximately **65–70 beats/minute**.
- **Mild ST elevation with prominent T waves in V2–V3**.
- No convincing reciprocal ST depression.

This could represent early repolarization, but **early anterior coronary occlusion remains a concern**, particularly if the changes are new or accompanied by symptoms. STEMI criteria depend on the ST elevation measured at the J point, including age- and sex-specific thresholds in V2–V3. [ACS guideline](https://www.jacc.org/doi/10.1016/j.jacc.2024.11.009)

**If there is current chest discomfort, breathlessness, sweating, or faintness, call emergency services now.** This needs immediate clinical assessment, comparison with prior ECGs, repeat ECGs, and troponin testing; a single tracing cannot rule out a heart attack.

What is the person’s age, sex, and symptom history—including when symptoms began?
